_note: Scripted replay for development and demos without a Meta API key. Runs that use it are labelled 'replay'. The first candidate is a deliberately naive filter of the reported strings, so that the held-out attacks are exercised; the second binds the pattern. Neither is model output.

facts.statement: The reported attack requests return products that do not match the query, and user email addresses, from the original service.
search_products builds its SQL text with format!, placing the query inside a quoted ILIKE pattern.

hypotheses.statement: The query text is interpolated into the SQL string, so a quote ends the literal and the rest of the query is parsed as SQL; binding the pattern as a parameter removes the injection.

missing_information: Whether other endpoints build SQL the same way
content.priority: Stop interpolating the search query into SQL text without changing ordinary search results.

content.hypothesis: Refusing queries that contain the reported attack strings stops the injection.
content.expected_effect: The reported attacks return no products.
content.falsified_if: Any attack still returns data, or any golden response changes.

patch.summary: Refuses queries that contain the reported attack strings (' OR ', 'UNION') and leaves the SQL as it is.

content.hypothesis: The query is interpolated into the SQL text; passing the ILIKE pattern as a bind parameter fixes the cause, so every variant of the attack fails.
content.expected_effect: Every attack, including variants, returns no products; ordinary searches return the same results.
content.falsified_if: Any attack still returns data or a server error, or any golden response changes.

patch.summary: Pass the search pattern as a bind parameter instead of placing the query in the SQL text.
